High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Applicant :- Mithlesh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Jitendra Prasad Mishra,Pulkit
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Jitendra Prasad Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ram Mohit Yadav,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 114 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Pailani, District-Banda, during the pendency of trial.

4. As per prosecution story, the marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the deceased person as per Hindu Rites on 11.05.2022, and subsequent to it, the applicant and other family members are stated to have subjected the victim to cruelty for demand of motorcycle and a golden chain as dowry,
Mithlesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79674841/
1

thereby leading her to death on 20.05.2024.
5.
Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The FIR is delayed by about nine days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The cause of death is Asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging.

The inquest proceeding was conducted on the next day of the death of the deceased person and informant was present at the time of inquest proceedings and he has been arrayed as a Panch witness in the said proceedings.
There are general and omnibus allegations against all the accused persons.

The statement of two witnesses were recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and they have also not supported the prosecution story, as such,
it is clear cut case of false implication.
6. It is further argued by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no criminal antecedent of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 04.10.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the fact that there is delay of nine days in institution of FIR and there being general and omnibus allegations against all the accused persons and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant-Mithlesh, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence during trial.
(ii) The applicant shall not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

Order Date :- 10.7.2025 Karan (Justice Krishan Pahal)
